messages:
maya: Quick question — for the frontdoor proxy: how should we handle incremental (chunked) responses when a client disconnects and reconnects? Two options I'm weighing: short-lived replay tokens that let client resume mid-stream vs forcing a full retry. Thoughts?

alex: I like replay tokens for UX. Clients get near-instant resume instead of waiting for full regen. Implementation idea: issue a signed token on stream start that encodes (request_id, last_sent_offset, model_version, expiry).

liam: Security note: signed tokens must be tight TTL and bound to requester (ip or api_key). Otherwise replay could leak results across users. Also avoid putting PII in token payload.

devon: Operational tradeoff: storing per-stream state gets expensive. Rather than persistent storage for every live request, we could keep sliding window state in tiered cache: in-memory on node + redis for cross-node fallback. TTLs like 60s for mem, 5m for redis.

alex: Example header idea:

    X-Frontdoor-Replay: eyJpZCI6IjEyMyIsIm9mZiI6NTAwfQ==

Server verifies signature, locates cached KV: redis.get("replay:123") -> {last_offset:500, checksum:...}

sam: Cost/scale: don't enable by default. Only for responses > 8k tokens or duration > 10s. Otherwise full retry is simpler and cheaper.

liam: Also consider partial-fallback semantics: if replay token missing/invalid, return 412 + body explaining client can either retry full or start a new request with same idempotency key.

devon: For long-running model calls, we should multiplex replay metadata into our existing prefix/KV cache. That reduces extra writes. But need eviction hooks when model version rolls.

maya: SDK UX question — how does client know when to attach replay token? Server should return token in trailers or initial 2xx chunk. Something like:

    {"event":"resume_token","token":"..."}

Client stores and retries automatically.

sam: Metrics: track replay-success, replay-failure, state-hit-rate, avg-latency-with-resume. Make replay_failure create an alert if >5% for long requests.

liam: Edge case: if the model output is non-deterministic (sampling), resuming may produce divergence. We must guarantee replay only when we can deterministically rehydrate KV cache. Otherwise force full redo.

maya: Good point — add requirement: replay allowed only for deterministically served backends or when we persist KV checkpoints. I'll draft constraints in RFC.

infra-bot: ci/cd: maya/rfc-frontdoor-replay created draft branch: refs/heads/rfc/frontdoor-replay-2026

maya: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC (scope: token format, TTLs, cache tiers, SDK surface, metrics). @alex take token signing, @devon design caching eviction, @sam run cost model. Ping me here when short PoC is ready. :+1:
